title: 5 Real-World MCP Servers You Can Use Today

cases.name: Filesystem MCP
cases.description: File and directory operations with access control

installation.explanation: Provides sandboxed file access within specified directory root

realWorldExample.userQuery: Find all TODO comments in the src/ directory and list them
realWorldExample.claudeAction: Uses list_dir and read_file tools to scan all files, parses for TODO pattern
realWorldExample.result: Returns organized list of TODO items with line numbers and files

setupInstructions: 1. Choose a root directory (e.g., /home/user/projects)
2. Run: claude mcp add filesystem -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /home/user/projects
3. Verify: /mcp (should show 'filesystem' in list)
4. Test: Ask Claude to list files in your project

commonErrors.cause: MCP process doesn't have read permissions
commonErrors.solution: chmod +r /path or use subdirectory with proper permissions

commonErrors.cause: Trying to access directory outside root sandbox
commonErrors.solution: Root directory sandboxes access; use path relative to root specified in installation

cases.name: GitHub MCP (Official)
cases.description: Repository, issue, PR, and workflow management for GitHub

installation.command: claude mcp add github -- docker run -e GITHUB_TOKEN=$GITHUB_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server
alternatives: npm package available but deprecated as of April 2025; Docker is official
installation.explanation: Requires GitHub Personal Access Token for API authentication

realWorldExample.userQuery: Search for all open bugs in my 'claude-code-mastery' repo and summarize by priority
realWorldExample.claudeAction: Uses search_issues to find issues with 'bug' label, filters by 'open' status, extracts priority from labels
realWorldExample.result: Returns organized list: 3 critical bugs, 5 high priority, 2 medium

setupInstructions: 1. Create GitHub Personal Access Token:
- Go to github.com → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens
- Select scopes: repo (full control), read:org
- Copy token
2. Set environment variable: export GITHUB_TOKEN='your_token'
3. Install Docker if not present
4. Run: claude mcp add github -- docker run -e GITHUB_TOKEN=$GITHUB_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server
5. Verify: /mcp (should show 'github' in list)
6. Test: Ask Claude to list open issues in one of your repos

commonErrors.cause: Token environment variable missing or token revoked
commonErrors.solution: Verify token exists with: echo $GITHUB_TOKEN; create new token if needed

commonErrors.cause: Repository doesn't exist or token lacks permissions
commonErrors.solution: Verify repo exists and token has 'repo' scope

commonErrors.cause: Too many API calls within rate limit window
commonErrors.solution: Wait 1 hour or upgrade to higher-tier GitHub account

cases.name: Memory MCP
cases.description: Persistent knowledge graph for cross-session context storage

installation.explanation: Stores entities, relations, and observations in JSONL format for persistence across sessions

realWorldExample.userQuery: Remember that Alice is working on the dashboard feature. She's blocked by the API changes.
realWorldExample.claudeAction: Creates entity 'Alice' (person), entity 'dashboard feature' (project), relation 'is_working_on', observation 'blocked_by_api_changes'
realWorldExample.result: Next session: 'What's Alice working on?' → 'Alice is working on dashboard feature, blocked by API changes'

setupInstructions: 1. Run: claude mcp add memory -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
2. Verify: /mcp (should show 'memory' in list)
3. Add knowledge: Tell Claude 'Remember: X is Y because Z'
4. Query knowledge: 'What do you know about X?'
5. Database file: ~/.claude-memory.jsonl (human-readable JSON lines)

commonErrors.cause: File permissions or directory doesn't exist
commonErrors.solution: Create directory and set permissions: mkdir -p ~/.claude; chmod 755 ~/.claude

useCases: Cross-session project context (remember what you were working on)
Architectural decisions (remember 'we chose X because Y')

cases.name: Fetch MCP
cases.description: Web content retrieval and HTML-to-Markdown conversion

installation.command: claude mcp add fetch -- uvx mcp-server-fetch
installation.explanation: Fetches and processes web content, converts HTML to readable Markdown

tools.name: fetch
tools.desc: Fetch URL and convert to Markdown

tools.name: fetch_with_chunks
tools.desc: Fetch and split into configurable chunks

realWorldExample.userQuery: What's in the latest Model Context Protocol announcement?
realWorldExample.claudeAction: Uses fetch tool on https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/, converts HTML to Markdown
realWorldExample.result: Returns formatted article content ready for analysis

setupInstructions: 1. Run: claude mcp add fetch -- uvx mcp-server-fetch
2. (Optional) Configure allowed domains in .mcp.json
3. Test: Ask Claude to fetch and summarize a URL

commonErrors.cause: Server blocks automated access or requires authentication
commonErrors.solution: Some APIs require API keys; use GitHub token or similar in ALLOWED_DOMAINS config
Use fetch_with_chunks to retrieve in configurable segments

cases.securityNote: Can access local IPs (http://localhost); be careful exposing private services

cases.name: Time MCP (Bonus)
cases.description: Timezone conversions and current time queries

installation.command: claude mcp add time -- uvx mcp-server-time
installation.explanation: Lightweight utility for time operations across timezones

realWorldExample.userQuery: What time is it in Tokyo when it's 9 AM in New York?
realWorldExample.result: 10 PM same day (or next day depending on daylight saving)

setupInstructions: 1. Run: claude mcp add time -- uvx mcp-server-time
2. Test: 'What time is it right now in London?'

steps.title: Prepare Credentials (if needed)
steps.details: For GitHub: Create Personal Access Token. For others: Check docstring.

steps.title: Add MCP
steps.example: claude mcp add github -- docker run -e GITHUB_TOKEN=$GITHUB_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server

steps.title: Verify Installation
steps.expectation: Should list installed MCPs including the new one

steps.title: Test Functionality
steps.action: Ask Claude to use the MCP tools
steps.example: For GitHub: 'List my open pull requests'; For Filesystem: 'Find all Python files'

bestPractices: Start with Filesystem and Memory MCPs (no external credentials needed)
Use GitHub MCP for repository management workflows
Combine multiple MCPs for complex workflows (e.g., fetch content + memory storage)
Monitor API rate limits when using external MCPs (GitHub, etc)
Store credentials as environment variables, never hardcoded
Test with /mcp list to verify all servers are healthy before intensive use
